title: Platform Governance in the Presence of Within-Complementor Interdependencies: Evidence from the Rideshare Industry
authors: Hyuck David Chung; Yue Maggie Zhou; Sendil K. Ethiraj
eligible_reason: Two single-date events, each analyzed in its own sample: Lyft's driver access restriction (LAR, June 27, 2019) and Uber's (UAR, later in 2019). Tables 2, 3 and 5 are before-after comparisons within NYC zones (LAR is a calendar-time post dummy; zone, day-of-week and hour-of-day FE, no calendar-date FE). Table 4 and A3 are two-group DiDs with a single onset (NYC rideshare vs NYC yellow taxi, or NYC vs Chicago), with a time-varying 2018-baseline control. No staggered adoption.
design_notes: Rideshare-RegressionDo.do: Table 2 reghdfe ln_ub_trip/ln_ly_trip LAR [ln_*_2018 ln_yw_trip], a(pu_zone pu_day pu_hour), cluster pu_zone, +-4 weeks, weekdays; Table 3 same for UAR; Table 4 reghdfe ln_trip LAR RS DD ln_trip_2018, a(rs_zone LAR_wk pu_day pu_hour) (DD = RS x LAR) and NYC vs Chicago (DD = NYC x LAR); Table 5 by rush-hour segment; appendix windows, week dummies, hour interactions, duration outcomes.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One onset per analysis (LAR or UAR); never pooled.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Not staggered.
